breaking_news.headline: Here is how SpaceX could turn up in your current investments
breaking_news.summary: SpaceX stock hit the market last week. Here's how it could turn up in your retirement or investment portfolio.

breaking_news.headline: Alan Greenspan, the legendary former Federal Reserve chair, dies
breaking_news.summary: During his chairmanship, Greenspan was celebrated as possibly the best central banker in history. But later, his reputation was tarnished by the worst financial crisis since the Great Depression.

breaking_news.headline: Did you know? Alan Greenspan and Ayn Rand were close friends
breaking_news.summary: One of the most intellectually important relationships in the life of the late Fed chair Alan Greenspan was with his close friend, the formidable novelist and libertarian thinker Ayn Rand.

breaking_news.headline: When falling housing prices are good news — and when they're not
breaking_news.summary: Denver renters are celebrating falling housing costs. But sometimes cheaper housing is a sign of economic decline. How can you tell the difference?

breaking_news.headline: Is AI 'one big bubble'? Behind the tech sell-off
breaking_news.summary: Investors are selling off AI-related stocks as doubts are starting to surface over whether the massive spending on AI is worth the investment and whether it's "one big bubble."

breaking_news.headline: Congress passes the largest housing affordability bill in decades — and Trump cancels the signing
breaking_news.summary: President Trump canceled a signing ceremony for the bill Wednesday, saying Congress must first pass a strict voter ID bill.

breaking_news.headline: Meta plans to release AI-powered prediction market app, documents show
breaking_news.summary: The company is building an app separate from Facebook and Instagram where people can wager on the outcome of real-world events, using "play money."

breaking_news.headline: World Cup fans are missing games after their resale tickets fall through
breaking_news.summary: The ordeal has left fans forced to either miss out on a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity or scramble to find new tickets, often costing more and for worse seats.

breaking_news.headline: Israel and Lebanon sign framework agreement after US-brokered talks
breaking_news.summary: Hezbollah is not party to Friday's agreement, and previous ceasefires between Israel and Lebanon have still seen near-daily cross-border strikes.

breaking_news.headline: DR Congo takes Rwanda to international court over decades of conflict
breaking_news.summary: Kinshasa accuses its neighbour of committing various violations since the 1994 Rwanda genocide.

breaking_news.headline: Religion row as Texas makes Bible stories required reading in schools
breaking_news.summary: Critics say the new reading requirements infringe on religious freedoms and blur the separation of church and state.

breaking_news.headline: Europe's deadly heatwave breaks German record and halts public events
breaking_news.summary: Germany's highest ever temperature of 41.3C is recorded provisionally in Saarbrücken, over the border from France.

breaking_news.headline: Meloni and Trump: A very public fall-out that is proving very hard to fix
breaking_news.summary: Italy's PM was not long ago being called the "Trump whisperer", but their relationship has gone from public attacks to personal insults.

breaking_news.headline: Mother dies saving daughter in Venezuela earthquakes
breaking_news.summary: Héctor Bello wrote on social media that "you gave your own life for our daughter" in the quakes which killed at least 920 people.

breaking_news.headline: Venezuela earthquakes kill 920 people as international rescue teams arrive
breaking_news.summary: Hundreds are still feared trapped under the rubble, as families desperate for news.

breaking_news.headline: US strikes Iran after attack on cargo ship
breaking_news.summary: US Central Command says it has struck missile and drone storage facilities and coastal radar positions.

breaking_news.headline: Teens who hacked TfL were known to police years before cyber-attack
breaking_news.summary: Owen Flowers and Thalha Jubair were convicted for their roles in the attack, which led to large costs for Transport for London.

breaking_news.headline: Who could be the UK's next chancellor?
breaking_news.summary: The prime minister's resignation has fired the starting gun on the race to be in charge of the UK's finances.

breaking_news.headline: What's happening to petrol prices now oil is back to pre-Iran war levels?
breaking_news.summary: When the conflict began on 28 February, fuel costs jumped as the war disrupted the production and transportation of energy across the Middle East.

breaking_news.headline: Asia stock markets slide as tech shares slump
breaking_news.summary: Trading on South Korea's Kospi index was halted for the third time this week to prevent panic selling.
